title: Let the commits decide the version number
summary: Read the commits since the last tag, decide major/minor/patch from their Conventional Commit types, and cut the tag automatically — no version file, no arguments about the number.
mental_model: The version is a function of the commits in the range. A breaking change bumps major, a feat bumps minor, a fix bumps patch — and because it is computed, nobody can forget to do it or disagree about it.

steps.title: Nothing releasable yet
steps.why: Only a chore commit since the tag. The script returns the current version unchanged — a release that would contain no user-visible change should not get a new number.

verify.label: a chore-only range produces no version bump

steps.title: A fix bumps the patch
steps.why: One `fix:` commit in the range moves 1.4.2 to 1.4.3. The rule is mechanical, which is the point — the number now describes the change rather than someone's judgement of it.

actions.run: git commit -q -m "fix(api): reject a missing id" --trailer "Refs: ABH-301"

verify.label: a fix bumps the patch component

steps.title: A feature outranks a fix
steps.why: Add a `feat:` commit and the same range now bumps the minor and resets the patch. The highest-ranking change in the range decides, which is exactly how semantic versioning is specified.

actions.run: git commit -q -m "feat(api): add a list endpoint" --trailer "Refs: ABH-302"

verify.label: a feature bumps the minor and resets the patch

steps.title: A breaking change outranks everything
steps.why: A `BREAKING CHANGE:` trailer — or a `!` before the colon — forces a major bump regardless of what else is in the range. This is the signal consumers depend on, so it must be in the commit rather than in someone's head.

actions.run: git commit -q -m "feat(api)!: require a tenant on every call" -m "BREAKING CHANGE: get() and list_all() now take a required tenant argument." --trailer "Refs: ABH-310"

steps.expect: v2.0.0 — major bump, minor and patch reset.

verify.label: a breaking change bumps the major version
verify.hint: BREAKING CHANGE: in the body, or ! before the colon in the subject

steps.title: Cut the release
steps.why: Compute, tag, verify. Because the tag is annotated, it records who released it and when — and `git describe` immediately reports the clean version.

steps.title: Confirm the next range starts empty
steps.why: After tagging, `describe --abbrev=0` returns the new tag and the range is empty, so the script proposes no bump. The loop is stable — running the release twice does not double-bump.

verify.label: running the release again proposes no further bump

steps.title: Guard it in CI
steps.why: The rule only works if the messages follow the convention. A commit-msg hook locally and a CI check on the pull request are what make the computed version trustworthy.

write.content:
#!/bin/sh
# Reject any commit in the range that does not follow the convention.
base="${1:-$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)}"
status=0

for sha in $(git rev-list --no-merges "$base..HEAD"); do
  subject=$(git log -1 --format=%s "$sha")
  case "$subject" in
    feat*|fix*|docs*|refactor*|test*|chore*|perf*) : ;;
    *) echo "non-conventional: $(git log -1 --format='%h %s' $sha)" >&2; status=1 ;;
  esac
done

[ "$status" -eq 0 ] && echo "all commit messages follow the convention"
exit $status

actions.run: git commit -q -m "chore(ci): validate commit message format"

verify.label: a message-format check is committed alongside the version script
the release version was computed from the commits and tagged
verify.hint: BREAKING CHANGE in the range forces a major bump

verify.label: the computation is idempotent after tagging
both the version rule and its guard live in the repository
every commit in the release follows the convention

pitfalls: Squash-merging replaces the branch's subjects with the pull-request title. If that title is not conventional, the version computation silently sees a chore.
`BREAKING CHANGE` must be in the commit body as a trailer, or marked with `!` in the subject. A note in the pull-request description is invisible to git.
A shallow CI clone cannot find the previous tag, so the script falls back to v0.0.0 and proposes a wrong version. Fetch tags and full history.
Never keep the version in a committed file as well — two sources of truth will disagree within a month. Derive it from the tag at build time.
Tag after generating the changelog, so the changelog commit is included in the release it describes.
cheatsheet: the full message, for BREAKING CHANGE
publish the commits and the tag together
